strings.do.tree.archivedWhy: Nothing active is filed under this level — every memory here is archived
strings.do.tree.crossingWhy: Nothing is filed here; this level organizes memories that live in other branches
strings.do.tree.intro: Domains nest like folders: 'acme/x100/p200' puts a memory in p200, which sits inside x100, which sits inside acme. Ask about any level and you get everything below it too. A name in italics holds no memory of its own — only the levels under it do. The +n next to a count is what sits further down. A memory can also BELONG to further levels without living there, which is the "also here" column: that is how one subject cuts across the tree.
